title: fix(useThen): re-throw the original error when the body threw, not the proxy access error
description:
## .what

when a useThen body throws, every downstream access to its result throws the proxy own error, not the original one, so the cause never reaches the log.

checkable evidence, ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-bhrain, 2026-08-31, blackbox/review.refs-single.acceptance.test.ts (test-fns 1.15.7). all four failed assertions print:

    UnexpectedCodePathError: useThen: tried to access value before test ran
        at Object.get (test-fns/src/domain.operations/useThen.ts:31:15)
        at cli (blackbox/review.refs-single.acceptance.test.ts:75:20)

line 75 is a plain read of res.cli.stderr: the proxy getter, never the throw site. the body threw, the proxy swallowed the error, and each then block reports the proxy complaint.

## .why

a genuine defect and a transient flake present identically, so a reader cannot tell why an attempt failed, only that it did. this is a failhide at the harness layer.

## .shape of the fix

- when the useThen body rejects, store the error; on a later access, re-throw the ORIGINAL error (with the proxy message as context, for example via cause), never a replacement
- keep the current message only for the true case: access before the block ran at all
- clamp: a useThen whose body throws a named error; a sibling then that reads the result must surface that named error

note: the retry half of the same report (a SOME criterion that could not rescue a failed attempt) is covered by #71, fixed in v1.17.1.

caught in ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-bhrain .dream/v2026_08_31.fix.repeatably-some-does-not-protect-a-ci-run.md
